history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Sagod Jain Temple (Sagod Jain Teerth) stands on Sagod Road off NH-79 on the outskirts of Ratlam city. Visitor reviews describe a white-marble temple with pristine idols, dedicated to Lord Adinath, whose idol is locally claimed to be 1000 years old (unverified). It is a clean, peaceful place of worship where aarti is performed twice daily and locals pray every day. No sect (Digambara/Shvetambara), founding date, or trust history is documented online (verify).

town_description: Ratlam is a major city in western Madhya Pradesh and one of the country's biggest railway junctions on the Delhi-Mumbai corridor. It is famous for Ratlami sev, gold jewellery, and the Kalika Mata and Kedareshwar temples. The city hosts many Jain temples in and around it, including the marble Sagod Jain Teerth on Sagod Road off NH-79.
